Change a webhook's name, URL, events, description or environment. Asks on a terminal when no flag is
given. Moving a webhook to test asks first; --yes skips that.

A production webhook receives the purchase events of production keys; a test webhook those of store
sandbox and test purchases. Person events reach both.

Events: purchase.completed, purchase.refunded, purchase.revoked, purchase.transferred,
subscription.created, subscription.renewed, subscription.product_changed, subscription.cancelled,
subscription.uncancelled, subscription.expired, subscription.billing_issue,
subscription.billing_recovered, subscription.paused, subscription.resumed, subscription.transferred,
perk_access.granted, perk_access.revoked, person.deleted. purchase.*, subscription.*, perk_access.*
and person.* name a group, and all every event that is sent.

Usage:
  voidhash webhook edit [webhook] [flags]

Arguments:
  webhook  The webhook's name, URL or id

Flags:
      --description <description>  Its new note; "" removes it
      --environment <production|test>
                                   Which purchase events it receives from now on: production or test
      --event <event>              Every event it should receive from now on; repeat for each (can
                                   be repeated)
  -h, --help                       Show help for this command
      --json                       Print the API objects as JSON, for scripts
      --name <name>                Its new name
      --project <project>          Project to act on: its id, slug, organization/slug or name
                                   (default: this directory's project, then your default project)
  -q, --quiet                      Print only ids, one per line
      --url <url>                  Its new URL
  -y, --yes                        Make the change without asking for confirmation

Global flags:
  -d, --debug              Print each request and full error detail to standard error
      --no-color           Print without colors (also when NO_COLOR is set)
      --profile <profile>  Use a named config profile: its settings override the base config
                           (default: VOIDHASH_PROFILE)

Examples:
  voidhash webhook edit "Orders backend" --url https://example.com/v2/webhooks
  voidhash webhook edit "Orders backend" --event purchase.* --event subscription.*
  voidhash webhook edit "Orders backend" --description ""
